$comment: The core's contributions. Each feature adds contrib/<feature>.json; scripts/manifest.mjs merges them into package.json.

enumDescriptions: Run the opentide the extension carries (the default): the same version for everyone, nothing to install. Ignores an opentide on PATH or in the workspace's environment.
Run your own opentide: opentide.path, the workspace's environment, uv, then PATH. If none answers, the bundled opentide runs, with a notice.
opentide.runtime.markdownDescription: Which opentide runs. **bundled** (default): the module the extension carries, with no install. **installed**: your own opentide (`opentide.path`, the workspace's environment, `uv`, `PATH`); if none answers, the bundled one runs and the log says why. Setting `opentide.path` without setting this selects **installed**. A workspace's value applies only in a trusted folder; in Restricted Mode only the engine (WASM) runs, whatever this says.

opentide.path.markdownDescription: An `opentide` executable (run with `lsp start`, every feature) or an `opentide-lsp` executable (run with `--stdio`, editor features only). Setting it selects the installed opentide, unless `opentide.runtime` is set; it is tried before the other installed runtimes. Ignored in Restricted Mode.

opentide.interpreter.markdownDescription: A Python interpreter with opentide installed (`pip install opentide`). The extension runs the `opentide` script next to it, else `python -m opentide`: set this where the `opentide` command cannot run. When set, it replaces the Python extensions, `.venv` and `PATH` lookup for the workspace runtime. Ignored in Restricted Mode.

opentide.uv.usePin.markdownDescription: Run the opentide version the repository pins (`pyproject.toml`, `requirements*.txt`, `uv.lock`) with `uv tool run --from opentide==<pin>`. Tried before the workspace's environment. Ignored in Restricted Mode.

opentide.uv.path.markdownDescription: The `uv` executable for `opentide.uv.usePin`. Default: `uv` on `PATH`. Ignored in Restricted Mode.

opentide.wasi.enabled.markdownDescription: Allow the opentide module the extension carries (`opentide.runtime`: bundled) and the engine's fallback to it. It has no network of its own: the extension host makes the tenant requests (query, deploy, validate --live) for the editor and, with opentide 1.0.0-rc.3 or later, for MCP; a terminal or task has none, so use `opentide.runtime: installed` for tenant commands there. Off: your own opentide if one answers, else the editor features of the opentide engine (WASM) only. Ignored in Restricted Mode, where only the engine runs.

enumDescriptions: Run the bundled opentide through VS Code's Node (the launcher) wherever that can run, even with the WASM WASI Core extension installed; use WASM WASI Core only where the launcher cannot run.
Always run the bundled opentide through VS Code's Node.
Run the bundled opentide under the WASM WASI Core extension (`ms-vscode.wasm-wasi-core`) when it is installed, else through VS Code's Node.
opentide.wasi.host.markdownDescription: What runs the bundled opentide (`opentide.runtime`: bundled) in the extension's desktop host. `auto` uses VS Code's own Node, which starts faster on a large workspace (first problems on 1,000 rules: 4.5 s, against 10.6 s under WASM WASI Core) and needs nothing installed. Takes effect at the next **opentide: Restart Server**.

opentide.envFile.markdownDescription: A `.env` file, relative to the workspace folder, whose variables are passed to commands that contact a tenant (opentide reads credentials only from the environment). Ignored in Restricted Mode.

enumDescriptions: Use one warm `opentide serve` process when the runtime has it.
opentide.backend.serve.markdownDescription: How the extension runs opentide commands.

enumDescriptions: Ask the language server for the problems of closed files, except from an opentide older than 1.0.0rc3, whose server re-analyses every closed file on each request and stalls completion for seconds.
opentide.diagnostics.workspacePull.markdownDescription: Whether VS Code asks the language server for the diagnostics of the workspace's closed files (`workspace/diagnostic`). It does so again 2 seconds after each answer, and an opentide older than 1.0.0rc3 re-analyses every closed file each time, on the thread that answers completions: stalls of seconds at a thousand objects. With `auto` those servers are not asked, **so the problems of closed files leave the Problems panel for them**; the files you have open keep theirs, and `opentide validate` (on save, on startup, from the palette) still reports the workspace.

opentide.trace.server.markdownDescription: Traces the communication between VS Code and the opentide language server, in the `opentide Language Server Trace` output.
